scope: Main native HTTP chat system prompt, actual tool-definition selection, structured local context, and external CLI context boundary. This does not establish identical model reasoning or full Stagewise behavior.

sourceContracts.note: Profile-specific intro/soul, filtered environment domains, output protocols/aliases and authority fragments.
Browser chat profile explicitly enables browser, shells, sandbox, activeApp, log ingest, workspace, AGENTS, skills, memory, plans and fileDiffs domains.
Use native filesystem tools first, return after shell/sandbox, and read before targeted multiEdit.
Stop on plan write; combine baseline native tools with supplied host tools and filter unavailable null entries.
Path/color link syntax and product aliases are prompt contracts, separate from rendering support.
Separate ACP instructions and context/resource representation; does not directly reuse native tool prompt.

remainingGaps.gap: Dynamic structured browser/active-app state and environment events are not assembled in the native main prompt like source profile domains.
remainingGaps.native: src/runtime/AgentToolHost.cpp:27 supplies shell manifest only; browser tools must be explicitly queried.

remainingGaps.gap: Plans/memory/log-ingest environment contracts and stop-after-plan-write policy are not ported by this patch.
Native typed transcript path/color/tab/app handlers do not imply that the model has source-equivalent output protocol/alias instructions. This patch does not add that table.
The complete source soul/output style/host fragments are not copied wholesale; native authority policy intentionally keeps conversation instructions above file/skill content.

External renderer carries respected project instructions and explicit invocations only. It does not supply ADE native credential/broker APIs, the entire skill catalog, or source ACP MCP question bridge.
Source asks for parallel independent calls; native Engine tool execution is sequential. Prompt does not claim unsupported scheduling.
Provider/model selection, model-specific defaults and differing runtime capabilities prevent a promise of identical reasoning or output.
